references.text: Moses mentions his age of 120 years and says he can no longer go out and come in, in contrast to Caleb who still has strength to go out and come in.
Moses died at the age of 120, but his eyes were not dimmed and his strength was not diminished - a similar testimony to preserved strength in old age.
Caleb was sent by Moses as a spy from the tribe of Judah, on the day he refers to in his speech.
God promised that Caleb would enter the land because of his faithfulness when he was sent out by Moses.
Caleb reminds us that he was 40 years old when Moses sent him from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land.
Caleb says that the Lord has kept him alive for 45 years since Moses sent him, and now he is 85 years old.
The Lord renews strength so that youth is renewed like the eagle's - a theme of God's preservation of power.
Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall run and not be weary - God's gift of strength to His people.
